question: Which Stellar anchors serve a specific country or currency corridor, what do anchor-to-anchor costs depend on, and when should I build my own anchor instead?

golden.answer:
A grounded answer derives its named examples and status claims from the current LumenLoop corpus, then dates the roster so it is not presented as permanent. As of 2026-07-11, a live partner query requiring both on- and off-ramp capability returned six matches, including Etherfuse, CLPX, and FinClusive.

The dated example is illustrative: a later grounded answer should report what the same source basis supports at its own observation time while preserving the stable distinctions above.
keyFacts: Presents specific source-supported content as a current or dated observation.
Makes the as-of date visible for every changeable roster, status, version, or measurement.
An existing-anchor integration is usually the lower-risk first launch.
Building your own anchor requires licensing/compliance plus banking/payout relationships.
It also requires liquidity/float and SEP/API implementation.
avoid: Do NOT name a specific anchor-to-country/currency corridor pairing (e.g. 'anchor X currently serves country Y') as currently live without citing a dated source for that pairing.

Do NOT attribute MoneyGram's 200+-country corporate money-transfer footprint (all-rails boilerplate: 'over 200 countries and territories') to its Stellar USDC off-ramp — MoneyGram's own developer docs put the off-ramp at 174 countries (as of 2026-07; marketing rounds to 170+, older SDF material says 180+). Any figure in the 170-180 band traceable to MoneyGram/SDF is acceptable; 185+ or 200+ for the Stellar cash-out network is not supported by any source.
Do NOT confuse SEP-defined APIs with a guarantee of liquidity, licensing, or coverage.
Do NOT collapse this into a last-mile mobile-money payout how-to; this question owns corridor selection, cost structure, and build-vs-integrate.
Do NOT present a changeable current measurement without its provider, scope, and observation date; registered invariants and explicitly historical quantities are not current measurements.
Do NOT claim an unsupported memory account is source-supported corridor evidence.

Accept any Stellar-off-ramp figure in the 170-180 band with a MoneyGram/SDF source; punish 185+ and 200+ attributed to the Stellar cash-out network (unsourced anywhere). The conflation framing resists rot better than a bare number: the corporate footprint always exceeds off-ramp coverage. Secondary caution: the ON-ramp is only 30+ countries — don't let candidates conflate on-ramp and off-ramp coverage.
